svg.title: How MRC uses multiple paths
svg.desc: MRC sprays one connection’s packets across ECMP paths, handles loss at the endpoints, and only resends what’s missing.
svg.text: MRC sprays one connection’s packets across ECMP paths, handles loss at the endpoints, and only resends what’s missing.

g.text: Changing the hash input allows one connection to use several paths.
Packet 2 is delayed. Packet 4 is lost.
Feedback and loss-recovery timing guide the retransmission.

g.title: Packet 4 is dropped. The original never arrives.
Slot 4 stays empty until the retransmitted packet arrives.

svg.text: Illustrative packet numbers and UDP ports. SACK text summarizes receive state; it is not a literal wire-format field.
